title: Triangle Congruence & Proof
standards_support: Use triangle angle relationships and classification criteria to solve and justify geometric conclusions.
Use SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, and HL as sufficient conditions for triangle congruence when their hypotheses are satisfied.
Use corresponding parts only after congruence has been established and organize proof statements in a valid dependency order.
Apply isosceles and equilateral triangle theorems and their converses.
Use triangle inequalities to determine whether side lengths are feasible and to solve missing-side ranges.
Use perpendicular bisectors, angle bisectors, medians, and altitudes to identify and reason about classical triangle centers.
Construct viable geometric arguments and critique circular, incomplete, or visually unsupported reasoning.
mathematical_practices: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
Construct viable arguments and critique reasoning.
Look for and make use of structure.

u03-l01: Classify triangles by sides and angles.
Use angle sum and exterior-angle relationships.
Distinguish feasible triangle descriptions from inconsistent ones.
u03-l02: Match corresponding vertices and sides before naming a theorem.
Use SSS and SAS when their hypotheses are satisfied.
Reject SSA as insufficient general congruence evidence.
u03-l03: Distinguish ASA from AAS by side location.
Verify right-triangle conditions before using HL.
Explain why AAA establishes shape but not size.
u03-l04: Establish triangle congruence before invoking CPCTC.
Read correspondence accurately from congruence statements.
Write multi-step proof chains with reasons for each claim.
u03-l05: Use equal sides to infer equal opposite angles and conversely.
Solve isosceles/equilateral angle and side problems.
Use inclusive classification and equilateral/equiangular structure precisely.
u03-l06: Test feasible, degenerate, and impossible side sets.
Apply triangle inequality to construction and design constraints.
u03-l07: Match concurrency lines to circumcenter, incenter, centroid, and orthocenter.
Use equal-distance properties of circumcenter and incenter.
Use centroid 2:1 structure and reason about center locations by triangle type.

unit_evidence: Seven hardened printable lessons with 20-problem lesson evidence.
Foundation, Core and Extended practice pathways.
A 12-question mastery check drawn from a lesson-aligned unit bank.
Written corrections or targeted remediation when mastery evidence is incomplete.
Triangle-Center Construction & Congruence Defense applied investigation with proof and construction evidence.

assessment_expectations.automatic: Objective mastery-check responses may be scored by the local assessment engine.
assessment_expectations.human_review: Open proofs, constructions, corrections, explanations and project evidence may require teacher, mentor or qualified reviewer judgment.
assessment_expectations.mastery: Target is 80% on objective evidence or documented correction/remediation evidence demonstrating the missed skills.
assessment_expectations.policy_note: Automatically scored evidence and human-reviewed proof/construction evidence must remain distinguishable in records.
